# spell.yaml reference

A spell is the declarative definition of one ushabti (one agent instance): its
role, its instructions, its model, the fields (targets) it tends, the implements
(tools) it may use, its Ma'at (the desired state), and the policy for the weighing
(the safety gate every write implement must pass).

This page is generated from the `Spell` model in the `ushabti` package, so it
cannot drift from what the loader accepts. Two complete examples live in
[examples/spells](../examples/spells): [k3s-watcher.yaml](../examples/spells/k3s-watcher.yaml)
and [proxmox-watcher.yaml](../examples/spells/proxmox-watcher.yaml).

Check a spell before you run it:

```bash
ushabti check-spell path/to/spell.yaml
```

The loader rejects three things outright: a key it does not know, an implement
that is not registered, and a secret written into the file.

## Keys

### Top level

The declarative definition of one ushabti.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apiVersion` | `ushabti/v1alpha1` | **required** | Schema version. Always `ushabti/v1alpha1`. |
| `kind` | `Spell` | **required** | Always `Spell`. |
| `metadata` | map, see [`metadata`](#metadata) | **required** | Identity of the spell. |
| `spec` | map, see [`spec`](#spec) | **required** | What the ushabti does and how it is kept safe. |

### `metadata`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** | Name of the spell. The ushabti running it takes this name unless `USHABTI_NAME` says otherwise. |

### `spec`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `role` | string | **required** | One line on what this ushabti is for. The model reads this. |
| `instructions` | string | empty | Standing instructions for the model. |
| `model` | map, see [`spec.model`](#specmodel) | **required** | Which model answers a summons (a unit of work). |
| `fields` | list of maps, see [`spec.fields[]`](#specfields) | `[]` | The fields (targets) this ushabti tends. |
| `implements` | list of strings | `[]` | Names of the implements (tools) this ushabti may use. Anything not listed here is rejected by the weighing. |
| `maat` | list of maps, see [`spec.maat[]`](#specmaat) | `[]` | Ma'at: assertions about what healthy looks like. |
| `weighing` | map, see [`spec.weighing`](#specweighing) | see its section | Policy for the weighing, the safety gate every write implement must pass. |
| `vigil` | map, see [`spec.vigil`](#specvigil) | see its section | The vigil, the monitoring loop. |
| `papyrus` | map, see [`spec.papyrus`](#specpapyrus) | see its section | Papyrus, the append-only audit log. |

### `spec.model`

Which model answers a summons, and how to reach it.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | one of `anthropic`, `openai_compatible`, `fake` | **required** | Model provider: `anthropic`, `openai_compatible`, or `fake`. |
| `name` | string | none | Model name, usually an environment reference such as `${USHABTI_MODEL}`. Required for `openai_compatible`. The `anthropic` provider falls back to its default model when this is omitted or the variable is unset. |
| `api_key` | environment reference such as `${NAME}` | none | API key as an environment reference such as `${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}`. A literal value is rejected. |
| `base_url` | string | none | Base URL of the endpoint. Use it to point `openai_compatible` at a local server such as Ollama or vLLM. |
| `max_tokens` | integer, greater than 0 | none | Upper bound on tokens per model reply. Each provider has its own default. |
| `max_steps` | integer, greater than 0 | `8` | How many times the model may be asked for implement calls while answering one summons. |

### `spec.fields[]`

A target an ushabti tends: a K3s cluster, a namespace, a Proxmox node, a service.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** | Name of the field. A summons (a unit of work) refers to a field by this name. |
| `kind` | one of `kubernetes`, `proxmox`, `prometheus`, `service` | **required** | What the field is: `kubernetes`, `proxmox`, `prometheus`, or `service`. |
| `namespaces` | list of strings | `[]` | Kubernetes namespaces to tend. The Kubernetes implements refuse any other namespace. Only valid when `kind` is `kubernetes`. |
| `context` | string | none | Kubeconfig context to reach the cluster through when the ushabti runs outside it. Inside a cluster the pod's service account is used and this is ignored. Only valid when `kind` is `kubernetes`. |
| `nodes` | list of strings | `[]` | Proxmox node names to tend. Only valid when `kind` is `proxmox`. |
| `endpoint` | string | none | Base URL of the field, usually an environment reference such as `${PROMETHEUS_URL}`. |

### `spec.maat[]`

One statement about what healthy looks like.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | **required** | Identifier of the assertion, unique within the spell. |
| `description` | string | **required** | What healthy looks like, in plain language. The model reads this. |
| `field` | string | none | Name of the field the assertion is about. Optional when the spell has one field. |
| `observe` | map, see [`spec.maat[].observe`](#specmaatobserve) | none | The observation the vigil makes each tick. Without it the assertion is context for the model only and is never evaluated. |
| `expect` | map, see [`spec.maat[].expect` and `spec.maat[].omen`](#specmaatexpect-and-specmaatomen) | none | Condition that must hold. When it does not, the vigil raises isfet (drift: something is wrong now). |
| `omen` | map, see [`spec.maat[].expect` and `spec.maat[].omen`](#specmaatexpect-and-specmaatomen) | none | Early-warning condition. When it holds while `expect` still holds, the vigil raises an omen (a prediction that something will be wrong soon). |

### `spec.maat[].observe`

Which read implement the vigil calls to check an assertion.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `implement` | string | **required** | Name of a read implement listed in the spell. |
| `arguments` | map | `{}` | Arguments passed to the implement. |

### `spec.maat[].expect` and `spec.maat[].omen`

One comparison against an observation.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | empty | Dotted path into the observation, such as `status.ready` or `items.0.phase`. Empty means the whole observation. |
| `op` | one of `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge` | **required** | Comparison to apply: `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt`, or `ge`. |
| `value` | string, number, boolean, or null | **required** | Value to compare the observation against. |

### `spec.weighing`

How strictly the weighing treats write implements.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_run` | boolean | `true` | When true, write implements are recorded and never run. This is the default. |
| `require_approval_for` | list of strings | `[write]` | Implement names or kinds that need operator approval. `write` covers every write implement. |
| `max_actions_per_hour` | integer, at least 0 | `5` | How many write implements may run in any one hour. Further writes are rejected. |

### `spec.vigil`

How often the ushabti observes its fields.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `interval` | duration such as `500ms`, `60s`, `5m`, `1h` | `1m` | Time between vigil ticks, such as `60s` or `5m`. |

### `spec.papyrus`

Where the ushabti writes its audit log.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | path | `papyrus.jsonl` | Path of the JSON Lines file. `USHABTI_PAPYRUS_PATH` overrides it. |

## Comparisons

The `op` of an `expect` or `omen` condition is one of:

| `op` | The condition holds when the observed value is |
|---|---|
| `eq` | equal to `value` |
| `ne` | not equal to `value` |
| `lt` | less than `value` |
| `le` | less than or equal to `value` |
| `gt` | greater than `value` |
| `ge` | greater than or equal to `value` |

`eq` and `ne` compare any JSON value. The ordering comparisons need two
numbers or two strings. A boolean never equals a number, so `true` is not `1`.

## How Ma'at is evaluated

An assertion with only an `id` and a `description` is context for the model: it
is never evaluated. Add `observe` and `expect` to have the vigil (the monitoring
loop) check it on every tick:

1. The vigil runs the read implement named in `observe`.
2. It looks up `expect.path` in the result and applies the comparison.
3. When `expect` does not hold, it raises isfet (something is wrong now).
4. When `expect` holds and `omen` also holds, it raises an omen (something will
   be wrong soon).

Isfet and omens each raise one summons (a unit of work) when they first appear,
not one per tick. When the path is missing or the values cannot be compared,
the result is unknown and nothing is raised.

## Environment references and secrets

Any string in a spell may hold an environment reference written `${NAME}`. The
reference is kept as written when the spell is loaded and is resolved only when
the value is needed, so `check-spell` works on a machine that does not hold the
secrets. An unset or empty variable counts as not set.

A key named like a secret may only hold a single environment reference, never a
literal value. A key counts as a secret when one of its words is `token`,
`password`, `passwd`, `secret`, `key`, or `apikey`. So `api_key`, `apiKey`, and
`admin_token` are secrets, and `max_tokens` is not. This applies everywhere in
the file, including the arguments of an `observe` block.

```yaml
api_key: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}   # accepted
api_key: sk-live-123            # rejected: a literal secret
```

`check-spell` prints the resolved spell with every secret masked, and warns
about each referenced variable that is not set.

## Implements

These are the implements that ship with the `ushabti` package. A spell may
list any of them under `spec.implements`. Every implement is either `read`
or `write`, and a write implement only runs with a `PASS` verdict from the
weighing.

| Implement | Kind | What it does | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `noop.read` | `read` | Return the given arguments unchanged. Observes nothing real. | ready |
| `noop.write` | `write` | Pretend to change something. Changes nothing real. | ready |
| `kubernetes.list_pods` | `read` | List the pods in a namespace with their phase and readiness. Returns each pod, the count, `not_ready` (pods that are not running with every container ready, finished jobs excluded), the total restarts, and the reasons containers are waiting or have failed, such as CrashLoopBackOff. | ready |
| `kubernetes.get_deployment` | `read` | Get one deployment with its desired and ready replica counts. Returns the counts under `replicas`, `missing` (desired minus ready), whether it is `ready`, its conditions, and the images it runs. | ready |
| `kubernetes.restart_deployment` | `write` | Restart a deployment by rolling its pods. | scaffold stub, not implemented yet |
| `kubernetes.scale_deployment` | `write` | Set the replica count of a deployment. | scaffold stub, not implemented yet |
| `proxmox.node_status` | `read` | Get the status of a Proxmox node: uptime, CPU, memory, storage. | scaffold stub, not implemented yet |
| `proxmox.list_vms` | `read` | List the virtual machines on a Proxmox node with their state. | scaffold stub, not implemented yet |
| `proxmox.start_vm` | `write` | Start a stopped virtual machine on a Proxmox node. | scaffold stub, not implemented yet |
| `prometheus.query` | `read` | Evaluate a PromQL expression at a single point in time. Returns the samples with their labels, their count, and, when there is exactly one sample, its number at `value`. | ready |
| `prometheus.query_range` | `read` | Evaluate a PromQL expression over a time range. Returns one series per label set, each with its values and its first, last, min, and max, and, when there is exactly one series, those four numbers at the top level. | ready |

There is no shell implement.
